title: Generalized Determinantal Point Processes for Attraction and Repulsion with Distinct Interaction Kernels
abstract: arXiv:2610.12894v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Determinantal point processes (DPPs) model subset selection probability with repulsion, but many applications also exhibit attraction arising from pairwise relations or shared latent structures. Nonsymmetric DPPs (NDPPs) capture both effects, but their kernels are difficult to interpret and specify. We propose the determinant-ratio point process (DRPP), which models repulsion and attraction via a ratio of the determinants of two symmetric positive-definite kernels. This formulation preserves the feature-based interpretation of standard DPPs while allowing the two effects to be specified separately. Furthermore, we introduce an auxiliary-variable representation that enables efficient MCMC sampling and yields tractable expectation formulas for key statistics including the normalizing constant, which together facilitate maximum-likelihood learning. tldr: 提出行列式比点过程（DRPP），利用两个对称正定核行列式之比分别建模排斥与吸引，在保持特征可解释性的同时，借助辅助变量表示实现高效MCMC采样与最大似然学习。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes the determinant-ratio point process (DRPP), which models repulsion and attraction separately via a ratio of two symmetric positive-definite kernels, preserving feature-based interpretability while enabling efficient MCMC sampling and maximum-likelihood learning through an auxiliary-variable representation.
